ai_question: Could you walk me through why you need to take leave next week?
sample_pattern: Sure — I have a family commitment that I can't reschedule, so I'd like to take Wednesday and Thursday off.
common_mistakes: Overly literal translation instead of the natural collocation 'take days off'
follow_up_question: Have you arranged for someone to cover your responsibilities while you're away?
grammar_explanation_en: Use the natural collocation 'take + day(s) + off', and 'commitment' (not 'business') for a personal obligation.
grammar_explanation_vi: Dùng cụm tự nhiên 'take + day(s) + off', và 'commitment' (không phải 'business') cho việc riêng cần giải quyết.

ai_question: How far in advance should employees request leave in your experience?
sample_pattern: In my experience, it's best to request leave at least a week in advance so the team can plan around it.
common_mistakes: Using 'plan for it' instead of the more natural 'plan around it'
follow_up_question: What happens if someone requests leave at the last minute?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Plan around something' is a natural collocation meaning to arrange things considering that factor.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Plan around something' là cụm tự nhiên nghĩa là sắp xếp mọi thứ có tính đến yếu tố đó.

ai_question: What's the best way to break the news to your manager that you need unexpected leave?
sample_pattern: I think the best approach is to be upfront about the situation and explain the urgency clearly.
common_mistakes: Using 'direct' instead of the more idiomatic 'upfront'
follow_up_question: How did your manager react when you explained the urgency?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Be upfront about something' is a natural idiom meaning to be honest and direct from the start.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Be upfront about something' là thành ngữ tự nhiên nghĩa là thẳng thắn, trung thực ngay từ đầu.

ai_question: How do you make sure your work doesn't pile up while you're on leave?
sample_pattern: I hand over my tasks to a colleague and leave detailed notes before I go.
common_mistakes: Using 'give' instead of the professional collocation 'hand over'
follow_up_question: How do you choose who to hand your tasks over to?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Hand over' is the natural professional collocation for transferring responsibility to someone else.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Hand over' là cụm chuyên nghiệp tự nhiên khi chuyển giao trách nhiệm cho người khác.

ai_question: Have you ever had a leave request turned down? How did you handle it?
sample_pattern: Yes, once — I calmly asked for the reasoning and proposed an alternative date instead.
common_mistakes: Using 'refused' instead of the more natural phrasal verb 'turned down'
follow_up_question: Did the alternative date work out in the end?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Turn down' is a common phrasal verb meaning to reject a request, more natural than 'refuse' in speech.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Turn down' là cụm động từ thông dụng nghĩa là từ chối một yêu cầu, tự nhiên hơn 'refuse' khi nói.

ai_question: What's your company's policy on carrying over unused leave days?
sample_pattern: We're allowed to carry over up to five days into the next year.
common_mistakes: Using 'bring over' instead of the correct collocation 'carry over'
follow_up_question: Do most employees actually use that carry-over option?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Carry over' is the fixed collocation for moving unused leave to a later period.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Carry over' là cụm cố định chỉ việc chuyển ngày nghỉ chưa dùng sang kỳ sau.

ai_question: How do you strike a balance between taking enough time off and not falling behind at work?
sample_pattern: I try to plan my leave around slower periods so I don't fall behind on deadlines.
common_mistakes: Using 'find balance' instead of the idiom 'strike a balance'
follow_up_question: How do you identify which periods are slower at work?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Strike a balance between A and B' is a natural idiom for finding a compromise between two things.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Strike a balance between A and B' là thành ngữ tự nhiên chỉ việc tìm sự cân bằng giữa hai điều.

ai_question: What do you usually do to prepare your team before you go on leave?
sample_pattern: I brief my team on ongoing projects and make sure everyone knows their responsibilities.
common_mistakes: Using 'tell' instead of the more professional collocation 'brief'
follow_up_question: How long does it usually take to brief your team?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Brief someone on something' is the natural professional collocation for giving a concise update.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Brief someone on something' là cụm chuyên nghiệp tự nhiên khi cung cấp thông tin ngắn gọn.

ai_question: How do you feel about employees who take leave right before a big deadline?
sample_pattern: It can be frustrating, but as long as they've handed things over properly, it usually works out.
common_mistakes: Using 'become good' instead of the natural phrase 'work out'
follow_up_question: What would you do differently in that situation?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Work out' means to happen successfully in the end — a natural, common expression.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Work out' nghĩa là cuối cùng diễn ra suôn sẻ — cách diễn đạt tự nhiên, thông dụng.

ai_question: How should we approach the client's budget concerns in tomorrow's meeting?
sample_pattern: We should emphasize the long-term ROI and propose a phased payment plan to alleviate their financial pressure.
common_mistakes: Using simple words like 'good money back' instead of the collocation 'ROI'
follow_up_question: Do you think the client will accept a phased plan?
grammar_explanation_en: Use professional collocations like 'emphasize ROI' and 'phased payment plan' instead of simple, generic words.
grammar_explanation_vi: Sử dụng các cụm từ chuyên nghiệp như 'emphasize ROI' và 'phased payment plan' thay cho từ vựng thông thường.

ai_question: What's the best way to build rapport with a client you're meeting for the first time?
sample_pattern: I usually start with some small talk and show genuine interest in their business before diving into the agenda.
common_mistakes: Using 'make friend' instead of the professional collocation 'build rapport'
follow_up_question: How do you know when it's the right time to move on to business?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Build rapport' is the standard professional collocation for establishing a friendly, trusting relationship.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Build rapport' là cụm chuyên nghiệp chuẩn để nói về việc xây dựng mối quan hệ thân thiện, tin cậy.

ai_question: How do you handle it when a client pushes back on your proposal?
sample_pattern: I try to understand their concerns first, then address each point with data to back up our position.
common_mistakes: Using 'says no' instead of the natural phrasal verb 'pushes back'
follow_up_question: Can you give an example of data that changed a client's mind?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Push back' is a natural phrasal verb meaning to resist or object to a proposal.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Push back' là cụm động từ tự nhiên nghĩa là phản đối hoặc từ chối một đề xuất.

ai_question: What's your strategy for keeping a client engaged during a long presentation?
sample_pattern: I break the content into short segments and check in with questions to keep them involved.
common_mistakes: Using 'ask them' instead of the natural collocation 'check in'
follow_up_question: How often do you pause to check in with the audience?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Check in with someone' means to briefly interact to see how they are following — a natural collocation.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Check in with someone' nghĩa là tương tác ngắn để xem họ có theo kịp không — cụm từ tự nhiên.

ai_question: How do you follow up with a client after a meeting that didn't go as planned?
sample_pattern: I send a summary email addressing their concerns and propose next steps to move forward.
common_mistakes: Using 'talk about' instead of the more formal 'address'
follow_up_question: What tone do you try to strike in that follow-up email?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Address a concern' is more professional and precise than 'talk about a concern'.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Address a concern' trang trọng và chính xác hơn 'talk about a concern'.

ai_question: What's the most effective way to negotiate pricing with a demanding client?
sample_pattern: I try to find a middle ground by bundling services instead of simply cutting the price.
common_mistakes: Using 'half way' instead of the idiom 'middle ground'
follow_up_question: Have you ever lost a deal because you couldn't find that middle ground?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Find a middle ground' is an idiom meaning to reach a compromise both sides accept.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Find a middle ground' là thành ngữ nghĩa là đạt được thỏa hiệp mà cả hai bên chấp nhận.

ai_question: How do you make sure the client feels heard during a difficult conversation?
sample_pattern: I actively listen, paraphrase their concerns, and acknowledge their frustration before responding.
common_mistakes: Using 'listen good' instead of the correct collocation 'actively listen'
follow_up_question: How do you usually paraphrase a client's concern?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Actively listen' is the correct collocation for attentive, engaged listening in a professional context.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Actively listen' là cụm đúng để diễn tả việc lắng nghe chăm chú, có tương tác trong bối cảnh chuyên nghiệp.

ai_question: How do you prepare when you know a client meeting might get tense?
sample_pattern: I anticipate their objections in advance and rehearse calm, fact-based responses.
common_mistakes: Using 'guess what they say' instead of the professional term 'anticipate objections'
follow_up_question: What's an objection you often anticipate from clients?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Anticipate objections' is standard business vocabulary for preparing for pushback in advance.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Anticipate objections' là từ vựng kinh doanh chuẩn khi chuẩn bị trước cho sự phản đối.

ai_question: What do you do if a client asks a question you don't know the answer to?
sample_pattern: I admit I'm not sure and promise to follow up with accurate information as soon as possible.
common_mistakes: Using 'answer back later' instead of the natural collocation 'follow up'
follow_up_question: How quickly do you usually get back to them?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Follow up with information' is the natural professional way to describe providing a delayed answer.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Follow up with information' là cách diễn đạt chuyên nghiệp tự nhiên khi trả lời sau.

ai_question: What do you think makes a team meeting actually productive?
sample_pattern: Having a clear agenda and sticking to time limits makes a huge difference in keeping things productive.
common_mistakes: Using 'follow the time' instead of the natural collocation 'stick to time limits'
follow_up_question: What happens in your meetings when discussions go off topic?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Stick to' is the natural collocation for adhering to a plan, agenda, or limit.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Stick to' là cụm tự nhiên khi nói về việc tuân thủ kế hoạch, chương trình hoặc giới hạn.

ai_question: How do you handle a team member who dominates every meeting?
sample_pattern: I usually create space for others by directly inviting quieter members to share their input.
common_mistakes: Using 'give chance' instead of the natural collocation 'create space'
follow_up_question: How do quieter team members usually respond when invited to speak?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Create space for someone' is a natural collocation meaning to give someone an opportunity to contribute.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Create space for someone' là cụm tự nhiên nghĩa là tạo cơ hội cho ai đó đóng góp ý kiến.

ai_question: How do you keep remote team members engaged during meetings?
sample_pattern: We make sure everyone has a chance to speak and use interactive tools like polls to keep it lively.
common_mistakes: Using 'active tools' instead of the correct adjective 'interactive'
follow_up_question: What tools have worked best for your remote meetings?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Interactive tools' (not 'active tools') is the correct term for tools that involve participant engagement.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Interactive tools' (không phải 'active tools') là thuật ngữ đúng chỉ công cụ có sự tương tác.

ai_question: What's your take on meetings that could have been an email instead?
sample_pattern: Honestly, they're a waste of time — if there's no discussion needed, a quick update should suffice.
common_mistakes: Using 'is enough' instead of the more formal 'suffice'
follow_up_question: How do you decide whether something needs a meeting or just an email?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Suffice' is a more formal, precise verb meaning 'to be enough' in professional contexts.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Suffice' là động từ trang trọng, chính xác hơn nghĩa là 'đủ' trong bối cảnh công việc.

ai_question: How do you make sure action items from meetings actually get done?
sample_pattern: We assign clear owners and deadlines to each action item and follow up in the next meeting.
common_mistakes: Using 'jobs' instead of the standard business term 'action items'
follow_up_question: What happens if someone misses their deadline?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Action items' is standard business vocabulary for tasks agreed on during a meeting.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Action items' là từ vựng kinh doanh chuẩn chỉ các công việc được thống nhất trong cuộc họp.

ai_question: What's the best way to handle disagreements between team members in a meeting?
sample_pattern: I try to steer the discussion toward common ground rather than letting it become a personal conflict.
common_mistakes: Using 'same idea' instead of the idiom 'common ground'
follow_up_question: Have you ever had to step in and mediate a disagreement?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Find/steer toward common ground' is an idiom for identifying shared points of agreement.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Find/steer toward common ground' là thành ngữ chỉ việc tìm điểm chung để thống nhất.

ai_question: How often should a team touch base as a group?
sample_pattern: I think touching base once a week is enough to stay aligned without wasting too much time.
common_mistakes: Using 'contact' instead of the natural idiom 'touch base'
follow_up_question: What do you usually cover when the team touches base?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Touch base' is a natural idiom meaning to briefly connect or check in with someone.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Touch base' là thành ngữ tự nhiên nghĩa là liên hệ hoặc trao đổi ngắn gọn với ai đó.

ai_question: How do you keep meetings on track when the discussion keeps drifting?
sample_pattern: I gently redirect the conversation back to the agenda and note off-topic points for later.
common_mistakes: Using 'not related' instead of the standard term 'off-topic'
follow_up_question: Where do you usually note down those off-topic points?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Off-topic' is the standard term for something unrelated to the current discussion.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Off-topic' là thuật ngữ chuẩn chỉ điều không liên quan đến chủ đề đang thảo luận.

ai_question: What role do you usually play in team meetings?
sample_pattern: I usually take the lead on technical topics and let others handle the scheduling side.
common_mistakes: Using 'be the leader' awkwardly instead of the natural phrase 'take the lead'
follow_up_question: How did you become the go-to person for technical topics?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Take the lead on something' is the natural way to describe being responsible for a topic.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Take the lead on something' là cách diễn đạt tự nhiên khi chịu trách nhiệm về một chủ đề.

ai_question: How do you summarize a complex project update for busy stakeholders?
sample_pattern: I focus on the key milestones and flag any risks upfront so they can quickly grasp the big picture.
common_mistakes: Using 'show problems' instead of the professional collocation 'flag risks'
follow_up_question: How do you decide which risks are worth flagging?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Flag a risk' is standard business vocabulary for pointing out a potential issue proactively.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Flag a risk' là từ vựng kinh doanh chuẩn khi chủ động chỉ ra một rủi ro tiềm ẩn.

ai_question: What's the best way to deliver bad news in a status update?
sample_pattern: I lead with the facts, take ownership if needed, and immediately follow up with a plan to fix it.
common_mistakes: Using 'accept the mistake' instead of the professional phrase 'take ownership'
follow_up_question: How does your manager usually respond when you take ownership like that?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Take ownership' is professional vocabulary for accepting responsibility for an outcome.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Take ownership' là từ vựng chuyên nghiệp chỉ việc nhận trách nhiệm về kết quả.

ai_question: How do you keep your manager in the loop without over-communicating?
sample_pattern: I send a concise update once a week and only reach out sooner if something urgent comes up.
common_mistakes: Using 'tell everything' instead of the idiom 'keep in the loop'
follow_up_question: What counts as urgent enough to reach out sooner?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Keep someone in the loop' is an idiom meaning to keep them informed appropriately.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Keep someone in the loop' là thành ngữ nghĩa là luôn cập nhật thông tin cho ai đó.

ai_question: How do you present a status update when a project is behind schedule?
sample_pattern: I'm upfront about the delay, explain the root cause, and outline a realistic path to get back on track.
common_mistakes: Using 'main reason' loosely instead of the precise term 'root cause'
follow_up_question: What usually causes projects to fall behind in your experience?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Root cause' is precise professional terminology for the fundamental reason behind a problem.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Root cause' là thuật ngữ chuyên nghiệp chính xác chỉ nguyên nhân gốc rễ của vấn đề.

ai_question: What format do you prefer for giving weekly updates — written or verbal?
sample_pattern: I prefer written updates because they're easier to reference later and keep everyone accountable.
common_mistakes: Using 'look back' loosely instead of the professional verb 'reference'
follow_up_question: Do you think verbal updates have any advantage over written ones?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Reference' as a verb means to refer back to something later — precise professional usage.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Reference' dùng như động từ nghĩa là tham chiếu lại sau này — cách dùng chuyên nghiệp chính xác.

ai_question: How do you handle giving an update when you genuinely have no progress to report?
sample_pattern: I'm honest about the blocker and focus the update on what I plan to do to move things forward.
common_mistakes: Using 'problem' loosely instead of the precise project term 'blocker'
follow_up_question: What's a blocker you've faced recently?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Blocker' is precise project-management terminology for something preventing progress.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Blocker' là thuật ngữ quản lý dự án chính xác chỉ điều đang cản trở tiến độ.

ai_question: How detailed should a status update be for senior management?
sample_pattern: It should be high-level, focusing on outcomes rather than the day-to-day details.
common_mistakes: Using 'big level' instead of the correct term 'high-level'
follow_up_question: How do you decide what counts as a day-to-day detail versus an outcome?
grammar_explanation_en: 'High-level' is the correct term for a broad, summary-style overview rather than fine detail.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'High-level' là thuật ngữ đúng chỉ cái nhìn tổng quan thay vì chi tiết cụ thể.

ai_question: How do you make sure your updates don't sound repetitive week after week?
sample_pattern: I try to highlight what's genuinely new and connect it back to the bigger project goals.
common_mistakes: Using 'show' loosely instead of the more precise verb 'highlight'
follow_up_question: How do you tie weekly progress back to bigger goals?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Highlight' means to draw attention to something important — more precise than a generic verb like 'show'.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Highlight' nghĩa là làm nổi bật điều quan trọng — chính xác hơn động từ chung chung như 'show'.

ai_question: What do you do if your update reveals a mistake you made?
sample_pattern: I own up to it right away and explain what I'm doing to correct it.
common_mistakes: Using 'say sorry' loosely instead of the idiom 'own up to'
follow_up_question: How do people usually react when you own up to a mistake quickly?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Own up to something' is an idiom meaning to admit responsibility for a mistake.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Own up to something' là thành ngữ nghĩa là thừa nhận trách nhiệm về một sai lầm.

ai_question: Can you walk me through a project you're particularly proud of?
sample_pattern: Sure — I led a redesign that cut our processing time in half, which really boosted team morale.
common_mistakes: Using 'tell about' loosely instead of the natural collocation 'walk me through'
follow_up_question: What was the biggest obstacle you faced during that project?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Walk someone through something' is a natural collocation for explaining a process step by step.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Walk someone through something' là cụm tự nhiên khi giải thích một quy trình từng bước.

ai_question: How do you handle constructive criticism from a manager?
sample_pattern: I try to take it in stride and look for the actionable takeaway rather than getting defensive.
common_mistakes: Using 'accept it calm' instead of the idiom 'take it in stride'
follow_up_question: Can you give an example of feedback that changed how you work?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Take something in stride' is an idiom meaning to handle a difficulty calmly without being upset.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Take something in stride' là thành ngữ nghĩa là bình tĩnh đón nhận khó khăn mà không bực bội.

ai_question: What would your previous manager say is your greatest strength?
sample_pattern: They'd probably say I'm reliable and always follow through on my commitments.
common_mistakes: Using 'finish it' loosely instead of the professional collocation 'follow through'
follow_up_question: Can you share a time you followed through under pressure?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Follow through on something' is a natural collocation for completing what you promised.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Follow through on something' là cụm tự nhiên khi hoàn thành điều đã cam kết.

ai_question: Describe a time you had to think on your feet.
sample_pattern: During a client demo, the system crashed, so I improvised a manual walkthrough to keep things on track.
common_mistakes: Using 'think fast' loosely instead of the idiom 'think on your feet'
follow_up_question: How did the client react to your improvisation?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Think on your feet' is an idiom meaning to react quickly and effectively in the moment.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Think on your feet' là thành ngữ nghĩa là phản ứng nhanh và hiệu quả ngay tại chỗ.

ai_question: How do you prioritize tasks when everything feels urgent?
sample_pattern: I assess the impact of each task first and tackle the ones that unblock the most work for others.
common_mistakes: Using 'check' loosely instead of the precise verb 'assess'
follow_up_question: Can you give an example of a task you deprioritized and why?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Assess impact' is precise professional vocabulary for evaluating how significant something is.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Assess impact' là từ vựng chuyên nghiệp chính xác chỉ việc đánh giá mức độ ảnh hưởng.

ai_question: What draws you to this particular role?
sample_pattern: I'm genuinely drawn to the chance to work cross-functionally and grow into a leadership position.
common_mistakes: Using 'like' loosely instead of the more expressive phrase 'drawn to'
follow_up_question: What does growing into leadership look like for you?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Be drawn to something' is a more expressive, natural way to say you find something appealing.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Be drawn to something' là cách diễn đạt sinh động, tự nhiên hơn để nói mình bị thu hút bởi điều gì.

ai_question: How do you approach working with a difficult colleague?
sample_pattern: I try to find common ground and keep communication professional, even when we disagree.
common_mistakes: Using 'be nice' vaguely instead of the precise phrase 'keep communication professional'
follow_up_question: Can you describe a specific disagreement you resolved this way?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Keep communication professional' is a precise phrase for maintaining appropriate workplace conduct.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Keep communication professional' là cụm chính xác chỉ việc giữ thái độ giao tiếp đúng mực nơi công sở.

ai_question: What's a skill gap you're actively working to close?
sample_pattern: I'm working on improving my public speaking, so I've started volunteering to lead more presentations.
common_mistakes: Using 'weak point' loosely instead of the professional term 'skill gap'
follow_up_question: What progress have you noticed so far?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Skill gap' is standard professional vocabulary for an area needing development.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Skill gap' là từ vựng chuyên nghiệp chuẩn chỉ lĩnh vực cần được phát triển thêm.

ai_question: How do you hook your audience in the first minute of a presentation?
sample_pattern: I usually open with a surprising statistic or a quick story that ties directly into the main point.
common_mistakes: Using 'catch attention' loosely instead of the natural verb 'hook'
follow_up_question: What's an opening statistic that's worked well for you?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Hook' the audience is a vivid, natural verb for capturing attention right away.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Hook' the audience là động từ sinh động, tự nhiên chỉ việc thu hút sự chú ý ngay từ đầu.

ai_question: How do you handle a tough question you weren't expecting during Q&A?
sample_pattern: I acknowledge the question, buy myself a moment to think, and answer as honestly as I can.
common_mistakes: Using 'take time' loosely instead of the idiom 'buy myself a moment'
follow_up_question: Have you ever had to say you didn't know the answer?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Buy yourself a moment' is an idiom meaning to gain a short pause to think before responding.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Buy yourself a moment' là thành ngữ nghĩa là tranh thủ một khoảng dừng ngắn để suy nghĩ.

ai_question: What's your process for simplifying a complex topic for a general audience?
sample_pattern: I strip away the jargon and use relatable analogies to get the main idea across.
common_mistakes: Using 'remove hard words' loosely instead of the natural collocation 'strip away jargon'
follow_up_question: What's an analogy you've used successfully before?

follow_up_question: Has your brother seen how far you've taken it since then?

grammar_explanation_vi: 'Get into something' là cách diễn đạt tự nhiên nghĩa là bắt đầu thích thú với một hoạt động.

ai_question: How do you make time for your hobbies with a busy schedule?
sample_pattern: I carve out at least a couple of hours on weekends, no matter how packed the week has been.
common_mistakes: Using 'find time' loosely instead of the more vivid phrase 'carve out time'
follow_up_question: What do you sacrifice to make that time happen?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Carve out time' is a vivid phrase meaning to deliberately set aside time despite a busy schedule.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Carve out time' là cách diễn đạt sinh động nghĩa là chủ động dành thời gian dù lịch bận rộn.

ai_question: What's a hobby you've always wanted to try but haven't gotten around to yet?
sample_pattern: I've always wanted to try rock climbing, but I just haven't gotten around to it.
common_mistakes: Using 'not do yet' loosely instead of the idiom 'get around to'
follow_up_question: What's stopping you from trying it?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Get around to something' is an idiom meaning to finally find time to do something after delaying.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Get around to something' là thành ngữ nghĩa là cuối cùng cũng có thời gian làm điều gì đó sau khi trì hoãn.

ai_question: How has your hobby helped you outside of just having fun?
sample_pattern: It's actually taught me patience and helped me unwind after stressful days at work.
common_mistakes: Using 'relax' loosely instead of the natural verb 'unwind'
follow_up_question: What else has it taught you that surprised you?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Unwind' is a natural verb specifically meaning to relax after stress or tension.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Unwind' là động từ tự nhiên chỉ việc thư giãn sau căng thẳng.

ai_question: How do you stay motivated when you hit a plateau in a hobby?
sample_pattern: I try mixing things up, like learning a new technique, to reignite my interest.
common_mistakes: Using 'stop improve' loosely instead of the idiom 'hit a plateau'
follow_up_question: What technique helped you get past a plateau before?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Hit a plateau' is an idiom meaning progress has stalled after a period of improvement.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Hit a plateau' là thành ngữ nghĩa là tiến độ chững lại sau một thời gian cải thiện.

ai_question: How do you decide when a hobby has turned into something more serious?
sample_pattern: When I start investing real money and time into gear, I know it's become more than just a casual interest.
common_mistakes: Using 'spend money' loosely instead of the more precise verb 'invest'
follow_up_question: What's the most you've invested in a hobby so far?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Invest time/money in something' is precise vocabulary for committing significant resources to it.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Invest time/money in something' là từ vựng chính xác khi dành nguồn lực đáng kể cho điều gì đó.

ai_question: What's the social side of your hobby like?
sample_pattern: I've met some great friends through a local club that shares the same interest.
common_mistakes: Using 'group of people' loosely instead of the correct noun 'club'
follow_up_question: How often does your club meet up?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Club' is the correct noun for an organized group sharing a common interest.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Club' là danh từ đúng chỉ một nhóm có tổ chức cùng chung sở thích.

ai_question: How do you avoid burning out on a hobby you're passionate about?
sample_pattern: I make sure to take breaks so it doesn't start to feel like an obligation instead of fun.
common_mistakes: Using 'too tired of' loosely instead of the correct phrase 'burn out'
follow_up_question: Has your hobby ever started to feel like an obligation?
grammar_explanation_en: 'Burn out (on something)' is the correct phrase for losing enthusiasm due to overexertion.
grammar_explanation_vi: 'Burn out (on something)' là cụm đúng chỉ việc mất hứng thú do làm quá sức.
